@abualam002 It means "to undefine function", basically to remove the information that there is a function and roll back to the raw disassembly without any markings. As an opposite action to "define function" that would mark particular piece of disassembly as a function and will perform a corresponding analysis.
@xarkes What is "Immediate Base" referring to? Is this translatable?

There is a category of instructions executed by the CPU called 'Immediate' instructions. These instructions essentially assign directly a number to a register. When disassembled in Cutter, the immediate value (i.e. number) in the instruction can be altered by changing the base. If you do not know what a base of a number is, lets say that a number can be represented in various base. the base we use daily is base 10 (because numbers with 1 digit can be represented by 10 values, 0 to 9), but in computer science we sometimes need to change the base of these numbers to something else, because these constant values might represent some bitfields (base 2) or else like base 16 or 8.
I would translate this: "Set base of immediate value to..."

trans-unit.note: @xarkes Context please. Where and how is this used?

Refers to the topmost address of the memory arena. In this case, imagine a sorted list of numbers [5,6,7,8,9], "Top" refers to the highest number in the list (i.e. the last). Example of the view: https://imgur.com/a/3O2BtI8
@deroad Thank you for the reply. In that case translating it as "last" makes more sense to me. Is "last" used to refer to something else in the UI?

Hmmm not really because in computer science the data that we are talking about is seen as a tower where the lowest address is at the bottom and the highest at the top. If you prefer you can use the word `High/Highest`
@xarkes Next free what?
I guess it is the "Next free arena" but I think the initial text should be updated probably. cc @XVilka
Yes, it is the next free memory arena. on cutter is just an address.

essentially is like saying `next number is XXXXX` but in this case we are talking about `Memory Arena` which is a special structure used to allocate/free memory by the "operating system". I think the right name for this should be `Next free arena` https://stackoverflow.com/questions/12825148/what-is-the-meaning-of-the-term-arena-in-relation-to-memory
Screenshot for reference: https://imgur.com/a/3O2BtI8
@xarkes Last remainder of what? Last remaining unused memory block address?

no, is the name of a variable which is part of the GLIBC malloc code. From the source code it is `The remainder from the most recent split of a small request` which judging from the code means that it is the remain space of the used chunk of memory. In doubt do a literal translation with `remainder` as the mathematical remainder.
